back: A package of policies, usually agreed with the IMF and World Bank, that moves an economy towards the market: cutting spending, removing controls, devaluing the currency and selling state businesses.

front: What is a balance of payments deficit?
back: A situation in which a country spends more foreign currency on imports and debt payments than it earns.
The first policy statement of independent Zimbabwe (March 1981), balancing growth with spending on education, health and rural development.
The Zimbabwe Conference on Reconstruction and Development, held in March 1981, at which donors pledged large amounts of aid and loans.

front: When did ESAP begin, and who supported it?
back: 1991, with the support of the IMF and the World Bank.
The Zimbabwe Programme for Economic and Social Transformation (1996-2000), which replaced ESAP.
"Black Friday": the Zimbabwe dollar lost a large part of its value in a few hours.

front: Why did the economy struggle in the 1980s despite early growth?
back: Droughts, world recession, shortages of foreign currency, deficits, controls and regional instability.

front: Why is ESAP described as having a high social cost?
back: Job losses in manufacturing, user fees for health and education, higher prices and falling real wages.
